easy.def: To press and move something back and forth on a surface.
examples: Rub your hands to get warm.
I rub my eyes.
She rubbed the lamp.

more.def: To press something against a surface and move it back and forth.
examples: He rubbed his hands together to get warm.
Rub the stain with a wet cloth.
The cat rubbed against my leg.

easy.def: A soft, bouncy material that stretches.
examples: The ball is made of rubber.
Rubber stretches.
The tires are rubber.

more.def: A soft, stretchy material that is used to make tires, balls and boots.
examples: Tires are made of rubber, which grips the road.
A rubber band stretches.
Rain boots are made of rubber.

easy.def: Things you throw away.
examples: Put the rubbish in the bin.
The rubbish is smelly.
Dad took out the rubbish.

more.def: Waste things that are thrown away, a word mostly used in Britain.
examples: Workers cleared the rubbish from the park.
A man collected the rubbish each morning.
The street was full of rubbish.

easy.def: Broken pieces of stone and brick.
examples: The wall fell into rubble.
Rubble covered the ground.
The workers cleared the rubble.

more.def: Broken pieces of stone, brick or concrete left after a building has fallen down.
examples: The old wall fell into a pile of rubble.
Workers cleared the rubble from the road after the earthquake.
Children played among the rubble of the ruined castle.

easy.def: A rub with a hand or cloth.
examples: He gave the horse a rubdown.
The rubdown felt good.
The player got a rubdown.

more.def: A brisk rub of the body or a surface with the hands or a cloth.
examples: The coach gave the sore player a rubdown.
He gave the horse a rubdown after the race.
A quick rubdown with a towel dried the dog.

easy.def: A deep red jewel.
examples: The ring has a ruby.
A ruby is red.
She found a ruby.

more.def: A precious red stone that is used in jewelry.
examples: The queen wore a crown set with a large ruby.
A ruby shone like a red drop of light.
Rubies are rare and are often cut into sparkling shapes.

easy.def: A lot of loud, wild noise.
examples: What is that ruckus?
The ruckus woke me.
The kids made a ruckus.

more.def: A loud, noisy disturbance made by people.
examples: The kids made a ruckus in the backyard.
What is all this ruckus about?
The ruckus in the hall woke the baby.

easy.def: A flat part at the back of a boat that turns it.
examples: The rudder turns the boat.
He moved the rudder.
A rudder is at the back.

more.def: A flat part at the back of a boat or aircraft that moves from side to side to help steer it.
examples: The sailor moved the rudder to turn the boat.
A rudder at the back of the plane helps it turn.
The boat could not turn because the rudder was stuck.

easy.def: Pink or red in the face.
examples: His cheeks were ruddy.
Her face was ruddy from the cold.
The ruddy boy grinned.

more.def: Having a healthy red or pink color, especially in the face.
examples: Her cheeks were ruddy from the cold wind.
The farmer had a ruddy face from working in the sun.
The ruddy glow of the fire lit the room.

easy.def: Not polite.
examples: It is rude to interrupt.
He was rude to the waiter.
That was a rude thing to say.

more.def: Not polite, showing bad manners.
examples: It is rude to talk with food in your mouth.
The rude boy did not say thank you.
She apologized for the rude thing she said.

easy.def: Not being polite.
examples: His rudeness upset her.
Rudeness is not nice.
I said sorry for my rudeness.

more.def: Behavior that is not polite or kind.
examples: His rudeness upset the waiter.
She apologized for her rudeness to the guest.
Rudeness at the table is not allowed.

easy.def: To feel sorry about something you did.
examples: I rue the day I broke it.
He rued his mistake.
She rued telling a lie.

more.def: To feel sorry about something you did and wish you had not done it.
examples: He rued the day he lost his favorite toy.
She rued her choice to leave her coat at home in the rain.
They rued not packing a lunch for the long trip.

easy.def: A fancy folded collar worn long ago, or fur around an animal's neck.
examples: He wore a ruff.
The ruff is pleated.
The lion has a ruff.

more.def: A wide, pleated collar worn long ago, or a ring of long feathers or fur around the neck of an animal.
examples: The actor wore a white ruff in the play.
The bird has a ruff of feathers around its neck.
The queen's ruff was folded in stiff pleats.

easy.def: A rough, rude person.
examples: The ruffian shouted.
The ruffian pushed in line.
A rude ruffian.

more.def: A rough and rude person who may cause trouble.
examples: The ruffian pushed past the others in line.
In the old tale, a ruffian stole the baker's pies.
The ruffians were chased from the market.

easy.def: To make hair or feathers messy.
examples: The wind will ruffle my hair.
She ruffled the dog's fur.
Birds ruffle their feathers.

more.def: To make something less smooth or tidy, or to make someone upset.
examples: The wind ruffled my hair.
The bird ruffled its feathers to stay warm.
He ruffled his brother's hair and ran away.

easy.def: A frill on clothes.
examples: The dress has a ruffle.
There is a ruffle on her sleeve.
The ruffle is pink.

more.def: A strip of cloth gathered into folds to make a frilly edge on clothes.
examples: The dress had a ruffle on the sleeve.
A pink ruffle trimmed the bottom of her skirt.
The curtains had a white ruffle along the edge.

easy.def: A small carpet.
examples: The cat sleeps on the rug.
I sit on the rug.
The rug is soft.

more.def: A thick piece of cloth that covers part of a floor.
examples: The cat slept on the rug by the fire.
We read stories on the round rug.
A blue rug lay in front of the door.

easy.def: A team game played with a ball that is not round.
examples: He plays rugby.
Rugby is a team game.
We watched rugby.

more.def: A team sport in which players carry, pass and kick an oval ball to score.
examples: He plays rugby on a muddy field.
In rugby, players cannot pass the ball forward.
My cousin's rugby team won the match.

easy.def: Rough and uneven, or strong.
examples: The path was rugged.
A rugged coast.
A rugged truck.

more.def: Rough, rocky and uneven, or strong and able to handle hard use.
examples: We hiked along the rugged coast with its sharp rocks and cliffs.
A rugged truck can drive over rough roads.
The mountains were rugged and wild.

easy.def: To spoil or destroy.
examples: The rain ruined the picnic.
Do not ruin the surprise.
She ruined her shirt.

more.def: To damage something so much that it is spoiled.
examples: Rain ruined our picnic plans.
He spilled paint and ruined the rug.
Spilled juice ruined the new book.

easy.def: The old broken remains of a building.
examples: We visited the ruins of an old castle.
Ivy covered the ruin.
The ruins were old.

more.def: The broken remains of a building that has fallen down, usually old.
examples: We explored the ruins of an ancient castle.
Ivy covered the ruin of the tower.
Visitors walk through the ruins in Greece.

easy.def: Something that tells you what you can and cannot do.
examples: The rule is no running.
Follow the rules.
A class rule is to raise your hand.

more.def: A statement that tells people what they may or may not do.
examples: The rule at the pool is no running.
Every game has rules that all players must follow.
We made a rule that everyone helps clean up.

easy.def: To be in charge of a land.
examples: The king ruled for twenty years.
A queen ruled the land.
Kings rule countries.

more.def: To have the power to lead and make decisions for a country or group.
examples: The queen ruled the island for forty years.
Long ago, powerful kings ruled huge empires.
Who rules the country now?

easy.def: A flat stick with marks for measuring.
examples: I measure with a ruler.
My ruler is yellow.
I drew a line with a ruler.

more.def: A flat strip of plastic, wood or metal, marked with units, used for measuring and drawing straight lines.
examples: I used a ruler to draw a straight line.
The ruler is twelve inches long.
She measured the length of the leaf with a ruler.

easy.def: A person who rules a country.
examples: The ruler lived in a castle.
The king is a ruler.
A ruler of the land.

more.def: A king, queen or other person who rules a country.
examples: The ruler lived in a castle and gave orders to the people.
The king was a wise ruler who was loved by his people.
Long ago, the ruler of the land had a golden crown.

easy.def: A decision made by a judge or someone in charge.
examples: The ruling was fair.
The judge made a ruling.
We waited for the ruling.

more.def: An official decision made by a judge or another person in charge.
examples: The judge made a ruling and the case was over.
The referee's ruling was that the ball was out.
We waited for the ruling of the school board.

easy.def: A lively dance.
examples: We danced the rumba.
The rumba is fast.
She loves the rumba.

more.def: A lively dance with a strong rhythm that began in Cuba.
examples: We learned the rumba in dance class.
The rumba has a lively beat.
The band played a rumba.

easy.def: To make a low, deep sound.
examples: The thunder rumbled.
My tummy rumbles.
The truck rumbled by.

more.def: To make a long, deep, rolling sound.
examples: The thunder rumbled in the distance.
My stomach rumbled before lunch.
The heavy truck rumbled down the road.

easy.def: To search by moving things around.
examples: I rummage in my bag.
She rummaged through the box.
Dad rummaged in the drawer.

more.def: To search for something by turning over and moving things.
examples: She rummaged through her backpack for her key.
The children rummaged in the attic for old toys.
Dad rummaged through the junk drawer for tape.

easy.def: A story people tell that may not be true.
examples: I heard a rumor that we will get a new slide.
Do not spread a rumor.
The rumor was not true.

more.def: A story that is passed from person to person and may or may not be true.
examples: There was a rumor that school would close early.
A rumor spread that a famous singer was in town.
Do not believe every rumor you hear.

easy.def: A noisy fuss.
examples: There was a rumpus.
The rumpus was loud.
A rumpus broke out.

more.def: A noisy mess of fuss.
examples: There was a rumpus when the dog got loose.
A rumpus broke out in the playground.
The kids made a rumpus upstairs.

easy.def: To move fast on your legs.
examples: I run fast.
The dog ran home.
Do not run in the hall.

more.def: To move quickly on foot, faster than walking.
examples: The children ran across the field to catch the kite.
Cheetahs run faster than any other animal.
He runs around the track every morning.

easy.def: To work the way it needs to.
examples: The car runs well.
Water runs from the tap.
The clock is running.

more.def: To work or operate, or to flow.
examples: The toy train runs on batteries.
A small stream runs through the meadow.
Do not let the water run while you brush your teeth.

easy.def: Being sent from place to place without help.
examples: I got the runaround.
We got the runaround at the store.
The runaround was annoying.

more.def: A series of excuses or delays that keeps you from getting an answer.
examples: I got the runaround when I asked about the lost bag.
The clerk gave us the runaround, sending us from desk to desk.
The clerk gave us a runaround.

easy.def: A person or animal that has gone away and will not stay.
examples: The runaway dog ran down the street.
A runaway came out of the barn.
The runaway was found in the park.

more.def: A person or animal that has left home or escaped and is hard to catch.
examples: The farmer chased the runaway pony across the field.
A runaway was spotted near the edge of the woods.
The story is about a runaway who finds a new home.

easy.def: Out of control and moving fast.
examples: A runaway cart rolled down the hill.
The runaway ball bounced down the road.
We saw a runaway bike roll away.

more.def: Moving fast with no one in control of it.
examples: A runaway wagon rolled down the steep hill.
The runaway balloon floated far above the trees.
Firefighters stopped the runaway truck at the bottom of the road.

easy.def: A short list of the main facts.
examples: Mom gave us a rundown of the trip.
Give me a rundown of the rules.
The coach read a rundown of plays.

more.def: A short summary that goes through the main points of something.
examples: The teacher gave us a quick rundown of the day's plan.
He gave the visitors a rundown of how the museum works.
Before the game, the coach shared a rundown of each player's job.

easy.def: One of the steps on a ladder.
examples: I stood on a rung.
The rung is broken.
Climb to the top rung.

more.def: One of the steps or bars that you put your feet on when you climb a ladder.
examples: I put my foot on the first rung of the ladder.
The top rung was loose.
Each rung of the ladder is made of wood.

easy.def: A person who runs.
examples: The runner is fast.
A runner won the race.
The runners lined up.

more.def: A person who runs, especially in a race.
examples: The runner crossed the finish line first.
A runner stretched before the race.
The runners lined up at the start.

easy.def: Thin and flowing like water.
examples: My nose is runny.
The soup is runny.
The paint is runny.

more.def: Thin and flowing easily, like a liquid.
examples: The runny paint dripped down the paper.
The soup was too runny, so we added flour.
She had a runny nose from her cold.

easy.def: The smallest animal in a group of babies.
examples: The puppy was the runt.
A runt of the litter.
The runt grew big.

more.def: The smallest and weakest animal in a group of babies born at the same time.
examples: The runt of the litter was the smallest puppy, but she grew up strong.
The farmer took extra care of the runt of the pigs.
Though he was the runt, the kitten was the bravest.

easy.def: A long strip where planes take off and land.
examples: The plane is on the runway.
The runway is long.
The jet landed on the runway.

more.def: A long, flat strip of ground at an airport where airplanes take off and land.
examples: The plane rolled down the runway.
The runway lights glowed in the dark.
The jet landed smoothly on the runway.

easy.def: In the country, not in the city.
examples: We live in a rural area.
A rural road has few cars.
The rural school is small.

more.def: Having to do with the countryside, not towns or cities.
examples: We live in a rural area with farms and fields.
The rural road had few cars.
Rural schools are often small.

easy.def: A clever trick.
examples: The fox used a ruse.
It was a ruse.
The ruse worked.

more.def: A clever trick used to fool someone.
examples: The fox used a ruse to get into the henhouse.
The sick cough was a ruse to get out of class.
Her ruse fooled everyone at the party.

easy.def: To hurry.
examples: Do not rush.
We rushed to the bus.
She rushes to school.

more.def: To move or do something very quickly.
examples: We rushed to catch the bus.
Water rushed down the stream.
Don't rush; there is plenty of time.

easy.def: A hurry.
examples: There is no rush.
We were in a rush.
The morning rush.

more.def: A time when people are in a great hurry.
examples: There is no rush to finish.
We were in a rush to catch the train.
Traffic is heavy during the morning rush.

easy.def: A red-brown color.
examples: The leaves were russet.
A russet apple.
The fox has russet fur.

more.def: A reddish-brown color, like autumn leaves.
examples: The leaves turned russet in the fall.
The fox had a russet coat.
She picked a russet apple from the tree.

easy.def: The brown stuff that forms on old metal.
examples: The old bike has rust.
Rust is on the gate.
I rubbed off the rust.

more.def: A reddish-brown coating that forms on iron or steel when it gets wet and stays damp.
examples: The old gate was covered with orange rust after years in the rain.
Rust can make a metal tool weak.
Dad scrubbed the rust off the garden shovel with a wire brush.

easy.def: To get covered with brown stuff, as metal does in water.
examples: The nail will rust in the rain.
My bike rusted.
Metal rusts when it is wet.

more.def: To get a reddish-brown coating, as iron and steel do when left in the wet.
examples: The bicycle rusted after we left it out in the rain all winter.
Iron nails rust quickly in damp air.
Dry the tools so that they will not rust.

easy.def: Covered with rust.
examples: The gate is rusted.
A rusted nail.
The rusted bike is old.

more.def: Covered with rust, the reddish-brown coating on old metal.
examples: The rusted gate creaked when it opened.
A rusted nail was in the old board.
The rusted bike sat in the shed for years.

easy.def: Simple and from the country.
examples: The cabin is rustic.
A rustic table.
We stayed in a rustic house.

more.def: Simple and plain, like things found in the country.
examples: We stayed in a rustic cabin in the woods.
The rustic table was made of rough wood.
The cafe had a rustic look.

easy.def: To make a soft sound like dry leaves.
examples: Dry leaves rustle.
The paper rustled.
The grass rustled.

more.def: To make a soft, dry sound like leaves or paper moving.
examples: Leaves rustle in the wind.
The paper rustled in my bag.
The tall grass rustled as the mouse ran through.

easy.def: A soft, dry sound.
examples: I heard a rustle.
The rustle of leaves.
A rustle in the grass.

more.def: A soft, dry sound made by things like leaves or paper.
examples: I heard a rustle in the bushes.
The rustle of leaves is a fall sound.
A rustle in the grass was just a mouse.

easy.def: Covered with rust.
examples: The gate is rusty.
The nail is rusty.
The old bike is rusty.

more.def: Covered with a reddish-brown coating that forms on iron when it gets wet.
examples: The gate was rusty and squeaked.
A rusty nail lay in the grass.
The old bike was rusty from the rain.

easy.def: A deep track in the ground made by wheels.
examples: The wagon made a rut.
The road has ruts.
I fell in a rut.

more.def: A deep track made in soft ground by wheels, or a boring habit that is hard to change.
examples: The wagon wheels left deep ruts in the muddy road.
The bumpy ruts made the ride rough.
He felt stuck in a rut doing the same thing every day.

easy.def: Cruel and without pity.
examples: The ruthless king was cruel.
A ruthless pirate.
He was ruthless.

more.def: Without any kindness or pity for others, and willing to be cruel to get what you want.
examples: In the story, the ruthless king taxed the poor villagers.
The ruthless pirate cared only about gold.
A ruthless fox sneaked into the henhouse.
